clue.text: Mature crowd retreats without casualties

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of outside: the crowd word sits round the casualties word
a crowd that retreats goes backwards, so its word is read from the end

parts.note: a mob is an unruly crowd
losses are the casualties of a battle

explanation.surface: A grown-up mob slinks away from a fight having suffered no injuries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside here, not lacking: the reversed crowd wraps round the casualties.
explanation.definitionFit: To blossom is to develop fully and flourish, as a person can when coming into their prime.

clue.text: Thomas and a maiden sitting under tree

indicators.note: in a down entry, sitting under places the following letters below the tree word

parts.note: a beech is a common tree
taken as written
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Someone called Thomas sits with a young woman beneath a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Thomas Beecham was a celebrated English conductor; 'Thomas' alone is the definition, by his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Thomas Beecham, founder of the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra, is a famous bearer of that first name.

clue.text: Vintage Roller always to be seen in the City?

definitions.text: Vintage Roller always to be seen in the City?

parts.words: Vintage Roller always to be seen in the City?
parts.note: surface reading: an old Rolls-Royce that is forever parked in the financial district

parts.words: Vintage Roller always to be seen in the City?
parts.note: setter's reading: an ancient thing that rolls on forever past the City of London, the river personified as an old man

explanation.surface: An old Rolls-Royce that is a permanent fixture in London's financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: A Roller is slang for a Rolls-Royce, but here it is something that rolls along: London's river, personified in folklore as an old man, flows past the City.
explanation.definitionFit: The personified river is old, rolls along endlessly, and runs through the City of London, matching each part of the clue.

clue.text: Mrs Mopp comes in to sweep — it means extra money

indicators.note: the cleaning lady comes in, entering the middle of the next word

parts.note: to surge is to sweep forward powerfully
Mrs Mopp was the charlady in the wartime radio comedy ITMA; a char is a cleaning woman

explanation.surface: The cleaner arrives to sweep up, which costs an additional fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweep' looks like the cleaner's job but is the outer word. Mrs Mopp is the British stock name for a charwoman, from the radio show ITMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcharge is an additional charge or payment added on top of the usual price.

clue.text: The number one commercial put on at end of day

indicators.note: being put on at the end of something means following it, so the day comes first

parts.note: Mon is the abbreviation for Monday
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: The top advertisement is broadcast as the day closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The number one' reads like a chart-topper, but it is the definition in its arithmetic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In philosophy and mathematics a monad is a unit, the single indivisible entity counted as one.

clue.text: Wants little boy to hug father

indicators.note: to hug is to wrap arms around, so the boy's name encloses the father

parts.note: Des is a shortened form of the name Desmond
a sire is a father, especially of an animal

explanation.surface: A small son longs to cuddle his dad.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are verbs of longing: if someone wants a thing, they desire or crave it.

clue.text: In depression ironclad company becomes inadequate

indicators.note: in places the whole iron-clad unit inside the depression word

parts.note: a dent is a small depression in a surface
Fe, the chemical symbol for iron, clad round ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, once a major British company

explanation.surface: During a slump, an armour-plated firm proves not good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ironclad' must be split: the iron symbol is clad round the company. ICI was Britain's big chemicals firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deficient falls short or lacks what is needed, so it is insufficient or not good enough.

clue.text: Stones set round small pudding

indicators.note: the stones are set round, placed about, the following word

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, a British unit of weight
wee is Scottish and informal for small

explanation.surface: Pebbles are arranged around a little dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a stone is 14 pounds, written st.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage the dessert course of a meal is called the sweet as well as the pudding.

clue.text: Oxford building in form of circle famed afar

indicators.note: the letters that follow are put into a new form, rearranged

parts.note: fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A well-known Oxford landmark is round in shape and famous far and wide.
explanation.walkthrough: The Radcliffe Camera is a domed circular reading room of the Bodleian Library, so the surface describes it truly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Radcliffe Camera is a domed eighteenth-century library reading room in central Oxford, part of the Bodleian.

clue.text: Marines rebuilt workshop

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Soldiers of the sea reconstruct a repair shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a group class or discussion session, like a workshop where participants study together.

clue.text: Frenzied men rode and fired gun in military campaign

indicators.note: frenzied means wildly agitated, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wild soldiers charged on horseback and shot their weapons during a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' only joins the two pairs of fodder words; its letters are not used.
explanation.definitionFit: Operation Enduring Freedom was the name of the American-led war in Afghanistan launched in 2001.

clue.text: Man who ran periodically in Kent, hot after race

definitions.text: Man who ran periodically in Kent

indicators.note: after places the hot letter behind the race word

parts.note: a heat is a qualifying race
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A runner who jogged now and then in Kent, sweaty after a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ran' means stood for election: Edward Heath, Conservative prime minister, contested his Kent seat of Bexley at general election after general election.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edward Heath was a British prime minister and long-serving member of parliament for a constituency in Kent.

clue.text: Look after little girl in squalid place — get a medal for it?

indicators.note: in places the combined letters inside the squalid place

parts.note: a den is a squalid or sordid place

indicators.note: after puts the look word behind the girl's name

parts.note: Cath is a short form of Catherine
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone cares for a small girl in a filthy hovel and is decorated for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' seems to mean care for, but it splits into the look word placed after the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The ten-event athletics contest is a sport in which an Olympian may win a medal, hence the question mark.

clue.text: A harem managed to accommodate an Eastern prince's wife

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house, so the rearranged letters take in the guests
managed suggests the letters have been organised, handled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for Eastern

explanation.surface: An Eastern ruler's wife is put in charge of the women's quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of the first two words is opened up between its fifth and sixth letters to take the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharanee is the wife of a maharajah, an Indian prince, or a princess ruling in her own right.

clue.text: Trader offering sink in Gloucestershire town

indicators.note: in places the sink word inside the town's name

parts.note: Newent is a small market town in Gloucestershire
to sag is to sink or droop

explanation.surface: A merchant sells a kitchen basin somewhere in the Cotswold county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sink' looks like a basin for sale but is a verb, to droop.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsagent is a shopkeeper selling newspapers and magazines, so a kind of retail trader.

clue.text: Gather at home with father round start of evening

indicators.note: with joins the home word to what follows

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: the father abbreviation goes round the selected letter

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: first letter of evening

explanation.surface: The family assembles indoors with dad as night begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gather' suggests assembling, but here it means to deduce.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to conclude from evidence, just as one gathers that something is so.

clue.text: At home, book is available if required

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: A book kept in the house can be lent out whenever someone needs it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' is a verb here, not the volume the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held in reserve is kept back for later use, ready to call on when needed.

clue.text: Goodly beer right for knocking back

indicators.note: the right letter is the one for knocking back, pushed further back toward the front, rearranging the word

parts.note: lager is a type of beer
names the R already in the beer as the letter that is to move; it adds no letters

explanation.surface: A decent pint deserves to be downed in one.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the R (right) moves: knocked back two places toward the front of the beer, the other letters keep their order. 'Knocking back' also plays on drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodly is an old-fashioned word for considerable in size, as in a goodly sum, meaning big.

clue.text: A little bit of pride?

parts.note: surface reading: a small amount of self-respect
setter's reading: a pride is a group of big cats, and a little member of one is its young offspring

explanation.walkthrough: Pride as a feeling gives way to pride as a collective noun for the big cats of the savanna.
explanation.definitionFit: A pride is a family group of lions, so a small member of it is a young one.

clue.text: A plant, or a tree, with flaw growing wild

indicators.note: growing wild means running untamed, so these letters are scattered into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some greenery, perhaps a tree, with a defect spreading out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterleaf is a North American woodland herb of the genus Hydrophyllum, so it is a plant.

clue.text: What one of the dukes may possess?

definitions.text: What one of the dukes may possess?

parts.words: What one of the dukes may possess?
parts.note: surface reading: the property or estate held by one of the nobility

parts.words: What one of the dukes may possess?
parts.note: setter's reading: dukes is slang for hands clenched to fight, so the question asks what one hand can hold

explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up your dukes' is boxing slang for raising your fists; the nobility are a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: The quantity a single closed hand can grasp is a handful of something, held in one fist.

clue.text: Onset of panic concealed by man surrounded by very big snakes

indicators.note: everything before is enclosed by the size word that follows

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing label meaning very big

indicators.note: by means next to, so the man stands beside what goes before
the onset of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of panic
hid is a past form of hide, to conceal
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: The first flush of fear is masked by someone hemmed in by enormous serpents.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophidians is the zoological term for members of the suborder of reptiles that comprises serpents.

clue.text: Foster in Gloucester, say, to enjoy deluge

parts.note: Doctor Foster went to Gloucester in the nursery rhyme; Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
to enjoy something can mean to have or possess it, as in enjoying good health

explanation.surface: Doctor Foster of the nursery rhyme goes to Gloucester and meets a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: In the rhyme Doctor Foster stepped in a puddle up to his middle in a shower of rain, which suits the deluge.
explanation.definitionFit: To deluge is to flood or overwhelm with water, as is to submerge or inundate.

clue.text: Sunday shop serving ice cream?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sunday
the Co-op is a chain of cooperative shops in Britain

explanation.surface: A store open on Sundays that sells ice cream.
explanation.walkthrough: The Co-op is a familiar British chain of grocery stores. 'Sunday' also hints at a sundae.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounded portion of ice cream served from a tub is a single ball or helping, called by that name.

clue.text: Sailor on board with his navigation system?

indicators.note: on board means inside a ship, written as the steamship letters around the sailor

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman aboard ship carries his own means of finding the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' does double duty, giving the ship's letters and placing the sailor inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors traditionally navigated by the heavens, steering by the positions of celestial bodies at night.

clue.text: Calm down — and don't let anyone else settle scores?

definitions.text: don't let anyone else settle scores?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: write the music scores yourself rather than having another composer do it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle scores' suggests revenge, but scores are pieces of music, and to compose them is to write them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an instruction to get a grip on emotions, and literally an instruction to write music personally.

clue.text: Helmet has function — that's admitted by cricketer

indicators.note: being admitted by someone means let inside, so the function goes within the cricketer

parts.note: a bat is a batsman, a cricketer who bats
sine is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A protective hat serves a purpose, as a batsman would concede.
explanation.walkthrough: Function is mathematical, not a purpose. In cricket a bat can mean the batsman himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A basinet was a light steel medieval headpiece, a close-fitting piece of armour for the head.

clue.text: Quiet rector confronts wickedness — a hidden triumph

indicators.note: the a is hidden inside the wickedness word
confronts means stands in front of, so the quiet and rector letters come first

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
R is the abbreviation for rector
evil is wickedness
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken clergyman faces down sin and wins a secret victory.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed grid's PEEVAIL is a misprint for the word the wordplay builds.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevail is to win or prove more powerful, as in good prevailing over evil.
